entries.body: The articles and opinions below, I, Ulrich Zwingli, confess to have preached in the worthy city of Zurich as based upon the Scriptures which are called inspired by God, and I offer to protect and conquer with the said articles, and where I have not now correctly understood said Scriptures I shall allow myself to be taught better, but only from said Scriptures.
entries.title: Introduction

entries.body: All who say that the Gospel is invalid without the confirmation of the Church err and slander God.
entries.title: Article I

entries.body: The sum and substance of the Gospel is that our Lord Jesus Christ, the true Son of God, has made known to us the will of his heavenly Father, and has with his innocence released us from death and reconciled God.
entries.title: Article II

entries.body: Hence Christ is the only way to salvation for all who ever were, are and shall be.
entries.title: Article III

entries.body: Who seeks or points out another door errs, yes, he is a murderer of souls and a thief.
entries.title: Article IV

entries.body: Therefore all who consider other teachings equal to or higher than the Gospel err, and do not know what the Gospel is.
entries.title: Article V

entries.body: For Jesus Christ is the guide and leader, promised by God to all human beings, which promise was fulfilled.
entries.title: Article VI

entries.body: That he is an eternal salvation and head of all believers, who are his body, but which is dead and can do nothing without him.
entries.title: Article VII

entries.body: From this follows first that all who dwell in the head are members and children of God, and that it is the church or communion of the saints, the bride of Christ, Ecclesia catholica.
entries.title: Article VIII

entries.body: Furthermore, that as the members of the body can do nothing without the control of the head, so no one in the body of Christ can do the least without his head, Christ.
entries.title: Article IX

entries.body: As that man is mad whose limbs (try to) do something without his head, tearing, wounding, injuring himself; thus when the members of Christ undertake something without their head, Christ, they are mad, and injure and burden themselves with unwise ordinances.
entries.title: Article X

entries.body: Hence we see in the clerical (so-called) ordinances, concerning their splendor, riches, classes, titles, laws, a cause of all foolishness, for they do not also agree with the head.
entries.title: Article XI

entries.body: Thus they still rage, not on account of the head (for that one is eager to bring forth in these times from the grace of God,) but because one will not let them rage, but tries to compel them to listen to the head.
entries.title: Article XII

entries.body: Where this (the head) is hearkened to one learns clearly and plainly the will of God, and man is attracted by his spirit to him and changed into him.
entries.title: Article XIII

entries.body: Therefore all Christian people shall use their best diligence that the Gospel of Christ be preached alike everywhere.
entries.title: Article XIV

entries.body: For in the faith rests our salvation, and in unbelief our damnation; for all truth is clear in him.
entries.title: Article XV

entries.body: In the Gospel one learns that human doctrines and decrees do not aid in salvation.
entries.title: Article XVI

entries.body: That Christ is the only eternal high priest, from which it follows that those who have called themselves high priests have opposed the honor and power of Christ, yes, cast it out.
entries.title: Article XVII: ABOUT THE POPE

entries.body: That Christ, having sacrificed himself once, is to eternity a certain and valid sacrifice for the sins of all faithful, from which it follows that the mass is not a sacrifice, but is a remembrance of the sacrifice and assurance of the salvation which Christ has given us.
entries.title: Article XVIII: ABOUT THE MASS

entries.body: That Christ is the only mediator between God and us.
entries.title: Article XIX: ABOUT THE MASS

entries.body: That God desires to give us all things in his name, whence it follows that outside of this life we need no mediator except himself.
entries.title: Article XX: ABOUT THE INTERCESSION OF THE SAINTS

entries.body: That when we pray for each other on earth, we do so in such manner that we believe that all things are given to us through Christ alone.
entries.title: Article XXI: ABOUT THE INTERCESSION OF THE SAINTS

entries.body: That Christ is our justice, from which follows that our works in so far as they are good, so far they are of Christ, but in so far as they are ours, they are neither right nor good.
entries.title: Article XXII: ABOUT GOOD WORKS

entries.body: That Christ scorns the property and pomp of this world, whence from it follows that those who attract wealth to themselves in his name slander him terribly when they make him a pretext for their avarice and willfulness.
entries.title: Article XXIII: CONCERNING CLERICAL PROPERTY

entries.body: That no Christian is bound to do those things which God has not decreed, therefore one may eat at all times all food, from which one learns that the decree about cheese and butter is a Roman swindle.
entries.title: Article XXIV: CONCERNING THE FORBIDDING OF FOOD

entries.body: That time and place is under the jurisdiction of Christian people, and man with them, from which is learned that those who fix time and place deprive the Christians of their liberty.
entries.title: Article XXV: ABOUT HOLIDAY AND PILGRIMAGE

entries.body: That God is displeased with nothing so much as with hypocrisy; from which is learned that all is gross hypocrisy and profligacy which is mere show before men. Under this condemnation fall hoods, insignia, plates, etc.
entries.title: Article XXVI: ABOUT HOODS, DRESS, INSIGNIA

entries.body: That all Christian men are brethren of Christ and brethren of one another, and shall create no father (for themselves) on earth. Under this condemnation fall orders, sects, brotherhoods, etc.
entries.title: Article XXVII: ABOUT ORDER AND SECTS

entries.body: That all which God has allowed or not forbidden is righteous, hence marriage is permitted to all human beings.
entries.title: Article XXVIII: ABOUT THE MARRIAGE OF ECCLESIASTS

entries.body: That all who are known as clergy sin when they do not protect themselves by marriage after they have become conscious that God has not enabled them to remain chaste.
entries.title: Article XXIX: ABOUT THE MARRIAGE OF ECCLESIASTS

entries.body: That those who promise chastity [outside of matrimony] take foolishly or childishly too much upon themselves, from which is learned that those who make such vows do wrong to the pious being.
entries.title: Article XXX: ABOUT THE VOW OF CHASTITY

entries.body: That no special person can impose the ban [excommunication] upon any one, except the Church, that is the [full] congregation of those among whom the one to be banned dwells, together with their watchman, i.e., the pastor.
entries.title: Article XXXI: ABOUT THE BAN

entries.body: That one may ban only him who gives public offence.
entries.title: Article XXXII: ABOUT THE BAN

entries.body: That property unrighteously acquired shall not be given to temples, monasteries, cathedrals, clergy or nuns, but to the needy, if it cannot be returned to the legal owner.
entries.title: Article XXXIII: ABOUT ILLEGAL PROPERTY

entries.body: The spiritual (so-called) power has no justification for its pomp in the teaching of Christ.
entries.title: Article XXXIV: ABOUT MAGISTRY

entries.body: But the laity has power and confirmation from the deed and doctrine of Christ.
entries.title: Article XXXV: ABOUT MAGISTRY

entries.body: All that the spiritual so-called state claims to have of power and protection belongs to the laity, if they wish to be Christians.
entries.title: Article XXXVI: ABOUT MAGISTRY

entries.body: To them, furthermore, all Christians owe obedience without exception.
entries.title: Article XXXVII: ABOUT MAGISTRY

entries.body: In so far as they do not command that which is contrary to God.
entries.title: Article XXXVIII: ABOUT MAGISTRY

entries.body: Therefore all their laws shall be in harmony with the divine will, so that they protect the oppressed, even if he does not complain.
entries.title: Article XXXIX: ABOUT MAGISTRY

entries.body: They alone may put to death justly, also, only those who give public offence (if God is not offended let another thing be commanded).
entries.title: Article XL: ABOUT MAGISTRY

entries.body: If they give good advice and help to those for whom they must account to God, then these owe to them bodily assistance.
entries.title: Article XLI: ABOUT MAGISTRY

entries.body: But if they are unfaithful and transgress the laws of Christ they may be deposed in the name of God.
entries.title: Article XLII: ABOUT MAGISTRY

entries.body: In short, the realm of him is best and most stable who rules in the name of God alone, and his is worst and most unstable who rules in accordance with his own will.
entries.title: Article XLIII: ABOUT MAGISTRY

entries.body: Real petitioners call to God in spirit and truly, without great ado before men.
entries.title: Article XLIV: ABOUT PRAYER

entries.body: Hypocrites do their work so that they may be seen by men, also receive their reward in this life.
entries.title: Article XLV: ABOUT PRAYER

entries.body: Hence it must always follow that church-song and outcry without devoutness, and only for reward, is seeking either fame before the men or gain.
entries.title: Article XLVI: ABOUT PRAYER

entries.body: Bodily death a man should suffer before he offend or scandalize a Christian.
entries.title: Article XLVII: ABOUT OFFENCE

entries.body: Whoever through stupidness or ignorance is offended without cause, he should not be left sick or weak, but he should be made strong, that he may not consider as a sin that which is not a sin.
entries.title: Article XLVIII: ABOUT OFFENCE

entries.body: Greater offence I know not than that one does not allow priests to have wives, but permits them to hire prostitutes. Out upon the shame!
entries.title: Article XLIX: ABOUT OFFENCE

entries.body: God alone remits sin through Jesus Christ, his Son, and alone our Lord.
entries.title: Article L: ABOUT REMITTANCE OF SIN

entries.body: Who assigns this to created beings detracts from the honor of God and gives it to him who is not God; this is real idolatry.
entries.title: Article LI: ABOUT REMITTANCE OF SIN

entries.body: Hence the confession which is made to the priest or neighbor shall not be declared to be a remittance of sin, but only a seeking for advice.
entries.title: Article LII: ABOUT REMITTANCE OF SIN

entries.body: Works of penance coming from the counsel of human beings (except excommunication) do not cancel sin; they are imposed as a menace to others.
entries.title: Article LIII: ABOUT REMITTANCE OF SIN

entries.body: Christ has borne all our pains and labor. Therefore whoever assigns to works of penance what belongs to Christ errs and slanders God.
entries.title: Article LIV: ABOUT REMITTANCE OF SIN

entries.body: Whoever pretends to remit to a penitent being any sin would not be a vicar of God or St. Peter, but of the devil.
entries.title: Article LV: ABOUT REMITTANCE OF SIN

entries.body: Whoever remits any sin only for the sake of money is the companion of Simon and Balaam, and the real messenger of the devil personified.
entries.title: Article LVI: ABOUT REMITTANCE OF SIN

entries.body: The true divine Scriptures know nothing about purgatory after this life.
entries.title: Article LVII: ABOUT PURGATORY

entries.body: The sentence of the dead is known to God only.
entries.title: Article LVIII: ABOUT PURGATORY

entries.body: And the less God has let us know concerning it, the less we should undertake to know about it.
entries.title: Article LIX: ABOUT PURGATORY

entries.body: That mankind earnestly calls to God to show mercy to the dead I do not condemn, but to determine a period of time therefore (seven years for a mortal sin), and to lie for the sake of gain, is not human, but devilish.
entries.title: Article LX: ABOUT PURGATORY

entries.body: About the form of consecration which the priests have received recent times the Scriptures know nothing.
entries.title: Article LXI: ABOUT THE PRIESTHOOD

entries.body: Furthermore, they [the Scriptures] recognize no priests except those who proclaim the word of God.
entries.title: Article LXII: ABOUT THE PRIESTHOOD

entries.body: They command honor should be shown, i.e. e., to furnish them with food for the body.
entries.title: Article LXIII: ABOUT THE PRIESTHOOD

entries.body: All those who recognize their errors shall not be allowed to suffer, but to die in peace, and thereafter arrange in a Christian manner their bequests to the Church.
entries.title: Article LXIV: ABOUT THE CESSATION OF MISUSAGES

entries.body: Those who do not wish to confess, God will probably take care of. Hence no force shall be used against their body, unless it be that they behave so criminally that one cannot do without that.
entries.title: Article LXV: ABOUT THE CESSATION OF MISUSAGES

entries.body: All the clerical superiors shall at once settle down, and with unanimity set up the cross of Christ, not the money-chests, or they will perish, for I tell you the ax is raised against the tree.
entries.title: Article LXVI: ABOUT THE CESSATION OF MISUSAGES

entries.body: If any one wishes conversation with me concerning interest, tithes, unbaptized children or confirmation, I am willing to answer.
entries.title: Article LXVII: ABOUT THE CESSATION OF MISUSAGES

entries.body: Let no one undertake here to argue with sophistry or human foolishness, but come to the Scriptures to accept them as the judge (for the Scriptures breathe the Spirit of God), so that the truth either may be found, or if found, as I hope, retained. Amen. Thus may God rule.
entries.title: Conclusion
